name: Orto-Tokoy Reservoir
near: Orto-Tokoy village — ~2 km from the dam (Asiamixtravel); Kochkor — ~20 km to the south; Balykchy — ~20 km to the northeast; the Kok-Moinok canyons — 20 km.
elev: About 1700 m above sea level (Wikijournal, Asiamixtravel); the water level changes by tens of meters with the season.
short: Orto-Tokoy is Kyrgyzstan's first artificial lake (1956–1960) on the Chu river between Balykchy and Kochkor: 18 km of turquoise water among bare hills, a convenient stop on the way to Song-Kol and Naryn.
desc: The Orto-Tokoy Reservoir was built on the Chu river where it leaves the Kochkor valley (construction 1941–1960, filling from 1956) to irrigate the Chu valley and southern Kazakhstan. Design parameters: volume ~470 million m³, area ~25–26 km², length ~18 km, depth up to 47 m, and a dam 52 m high and 365 m long. In spring the reservoir is almost full, and by the end of summer the level drops noticeably — in the low-water year 2023 the bottom was exposed (inflow 250 million m³ against 360 million in 2021). The color of the water ranges from soft blue to emerald and almost black depending on the stretch; around are treeless hills, and Bactrian camels graze along the shores. The A-363 road Balykchy — Kochkor runs along the north shore, so people mostly view the reservoir from the roadside and stop for a picnic; fishing (marinka, osman, trout, whitefish), camping and SUP are possible. There is no beach infrastructure, rental or lifeguards; walking on the ice is forbidden in winter.
guide: Don't plan a separate trip here — but don't just drive past either: on the road from Balykchy to Kochkor and Song-Kol, find a wide pull-off by the A-363 above the water, where the color shifts from turquoise to inky. It is best in spring and early summer, when the basin is full; by September the water recedes, and the exposed bottom with sticky silt looks bleak (in 2023 it showed completely). Look for Bactrian camels on the shore — they are grazed here. If you are going with a fishing rod, ask in Kochkor about spawning bans; nets are prohibited. For a night, choose shallow bays far from the road, and bring warm clothes — even in summer the water is rarely warmer than +15 °C.
see: The shore landscape of the reservoir on the Chu; the outlines of the shores and the color of the water change with the level — from turquoise to emerald; the dam (52 m) near Orto-Tokoy village; camels on the shore; spring high water and the autumn “terraces” of the exposed bottom; in winter — ice (walking on it is forbidden).
skip: You are not driving along the Balykchy — Kochkor road: as a standalone destination the reservoir is “not particularly memorable” (TripAdvisor reviews). Late summer/autumn of a low-water year — instead of a lake there will be silt and bare bottom. You need an equipped beach — there isn't one.
diff: Very easy: a stop by the road, a 50–100 m descent to the water down a slope; for camping — dirt turn-offs.
when: Spring — early summer (April — June): a full basin and green slopes; July — August for swimming (cold water) and camping; in autumn the level is low; in winter — photos of the ice, without walking on it.
hours: Open territory, around the clock; the dam is a hydraulic facility, and access to the structures is restricted (guarded by the Water Resources Service).
daytime: Morning and evening — calm water and color without glare; in the daytime the treeless shores are hot and windy.
how: From Bishkek through Boom Gorge and Balykchy, then along the A-363 towards Kochkor — the road runs along the north shore; ~190 km, 3–3.5 h. From Kochkor ~20 km north. Stop at the wide pull-offs by the road; the turn-offs to the water are dirt.
needcar: Yes: the reservoir is along the road, and without your own car — only in passing on a marshrutka (minibus)/taxi with a stop on request.
self: Yes: free access to the shores from the road; follow the roadside parking rules, don't approach the dam and spillway, don't walk on the ice, take your litter away; fishing — observing spawning bans, nets are prohibited.
roadtype: Paved A-363 along the north shore; turn-offs to the water are dirt, in places across the exposed bottom (sticky silt — don't drive onto it).
traveltime: Bishkek — reservoir ~190 km, 3–3.5 h; Balykchy — 20–30 min; Kochkor — 20–30 min; a stop of 15–30 min, picnic/camping — as you wish.
stay: On the shore — only wild camping (no infrastructure). The nearest accommodation: CBT Kochkor guesthouses and hotels in Kochkor (20 km), hotels in Balykchy (20 km). 2025–2026 prices are not confirmed.
net: Along the A-363 there is operator coverage (the settlements of Orto-Tokoy, Kok-Moinok, Kochkor); in bays behind the hills the signal weakens. There are no reports by operator.
entry: Free: sources mention no fees for access to the shore.
transfer: Train Bishkek — Balykchy 40–60 som (summer 2024); marshrutka Bishkek — Kochkor: the 2025 price is not confirmed (a guide — Bishkek — Karakol 500 som in 2024); taxi Balykchy — Orto-Tokoy by arrangement.
bring: A windbreaker (open shores), sun protection, water and food (there are no cafes by the water), a picnic mat, trash bags; for camping — a tent with good pegs (wind), for fishing — tackle and knowledge of the bans; warm clothes for swimming (+15 °C).
warn: The water level fluctuates greatly: by the end of summer and in low-water years (2023) the water recedes, and the bottom is sticky silt — don't drive or walk onto it. In winter walking on the ice is forbidden. The dam and spillway are a restricted facility. Park only at wide pull-offs, fully off the carriageway of the A-363. Cold water, sharp wind. Administratively this is Naryn Region — keep this in mind when planning routes and insurance.
food: There are no cafes at the reservoir. In Kochkor — CBT families with home cooking, beshbarmak, kumys in summer; in Balykchy and on the road — Issyk-Kul fish and roadside cafes (“Ak-Jol” at the turn to Kochkor).
reviews: Google Maps (“Orto-Tokoy reservoir”): 4.8/5, 76 ratings as of 03.10.2026. TripAdvisor “Orto-Tokoy Water Reservoir” (Kochkor, Naryn Region): 3.9/5, 10 reviews, No. 2 of 5 in Kochkor (07.10.2026). Pluses: bright blue water in summer, a good stop on a long drive, camels; minuses: “nothing special” unless you are passing through; no infrastructure.

p.sum: Orto-Tokoy is a photo stop by the A-363 Balykchy — Kochkor road (20 km to each, 20–30 minutes, ≈190 km from Bishkek). The road runs along the north shore; stop at the wide pull-offs. Without a car, any marshrutka Bishkek — Kochkor or Naryn will do (350–600 som, 2026): ask to be dropped off by the water. It is best in spring and early summer while the basin is full; by the end of summer the bottom may be exposed, as in 2023. For a night — wild camping in the bays or CBT guesthouses in Kochkor. Fishing is possible: in 03.2026, 1.2 million whitefish fry were released into the reservoir, and nets are prohibited.

p.season: April–June: a full basin, green slopes. July–August: swimming (cold) and camping, wind and heat in the daytime. September–October: the level drops, exposed shores are possible (in 2023 — the whole bottom). November–March: ice, walking on it forbidden; the A-363 road is open.
p.budget.economy: ≈800–2500 som/person: marshrutka Bishkek — Kochkor 350 with a drop-off, camping free or a guesthouse in Kochkor $21–36, your own food.
p.budget.comfort: ≈3000–6000 som/person: your own/rented car or a tour with a photo stop, a CBT guesthouse in Kochkor.
p.permits: Not needed for a visit. For fishing — an amateur fishing ticket (online issuance via MegaPay is so far described only for Issyk-Kul; for the reservoir, check with the Fisheries Department), nets are prohibited. The dam is a restricted facility.
p.access: The view from the pull-offs is accessible to everyone, including older people and people in wheelchairs (from the pavement). The descent to the water is down a slope. With children and a dog — yes, but be careful by the water (silt, cold).
